WITH RECURSIVE ancestry AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id, base_symbol_id AS ancestor, 1 AS depth
  FROM code.class_bases
  WHERE base_name = 'ApiModel'

  UNION ALL

  SELECT a.class_symbol_id, c.base_symbol_id, a.depth + 1
  FROM ancestry a
  JOIN code.class_bases c ON a.ancestor = c.class_symbol_id
  WHERE c.base_name != 'ApiModel'
)
SELECT class_symbol_id, MIN(depth) AS depth
FROM ancestry
GROUP BY class_symbol_id
HAVING MIN(depth) > 1
ORDER BY class_symbol_id;

request:
Which classes inherit from ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/models.py) only indirectly, i.e. through at least one intermediate class of this repository, and do not name ApiModel directly in their class statement? An import alias of ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/responses.py imports it as _Payload) counts as naming ApiModel directly, and a subscripted base such as ListResponse[T] counts as its class. For each, give the class symbol ID and the length of the shortest inheritance chain to ApiModel (2 when the parent class directly subclasses ApiModel).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
explanation: The recursive CTE starts by finding all classes that directly name ApiModel as a base (depth 1). It then repeatedly follows class_bases edges to find indirect subclasses, incrementing depth. The final SELECT groups by class_symbol_id, keeps only those whose minimum depth exceeds 1 (meaning they do not name ApiModel directly), and returns the shortest inheritance chain length.
